configurePresets.name: dev
configurePresets.description: The everyday build. Host default compiler, warnings on but not fatal.

configurePresets.name: dev-debug
configurePresets.description: Debug build. Also the compile database clang-tidy reads: tidy findings must be reproducible, and the database's flags depend on the configuration.

configurePresets.name: clang-release
configurePresets.description: CI gate. -Werror is calibrated against clang's warning set, so a new clang diagnostic is a change we want to see.

configurePresets.name: clang-debug
configurePresets.description: CI gate. Paired with clang-release because NDEBUG changes which variables are used and the optimizer's flow-sensitive diagnostics need -O2.

configurePresets.name: gcc-release
configurePresets.description: Proves the library compiles and passes with the other major toolchain, the one a distro package build uses. -Werror stays off: GCC's -Wconversion and -Wold-style-cast fire on different things than clang's.

configurePresets.name: gcc-debug
configurePresets.description: See gcc-release. Debug half of the same pair.

configurePresets.name: asan-ubsan
configurePresets.description: Debug, not Release: at -O3 the compiler inlines away the frames a sanitizer report is made of. ASan and UBSan share one build because they compose; TSan cannot join them.

configurePresets.name: tsan
configurePresets.description: Its own configuration because TSan and ASan use incompatible shadow memory layouts. Verifies the documented promise that the API is reentrant.

configurePresets.name: coverage
configurePresets.description: Source-based coverage. Debug, because an optimized build attributes an inlined line to its call site and reports coverage for source that was never separately compiled.

configurePresets.name: valgrind
configurePresets.description: Deliberately uninstrumented: Valgrind and the sanitizers both replace the allocator and the combination reports nonsense. Its own binaryDir is what keeps the two builds from sharing objects. Linux only; Valgrind does not run on Apple Silicon.

testPresets.name: sanitizer-common
testPresets.description: Serial regardless of core count: ASan and TSan each reserve a large shadow mapping per process, and eight at once on a CI runner is an OOM kill that looks like a test failure.

testPresets.name: asan-base
testPresets.description: Shared by the two asan test presets, which differ only in whether LeakSanitizer is asked for. UBSan aborts on the first finding either way -- the build passes -fno-sanitize-recover=all -- and a report is only actionable with a stack trace.

testPresets.name: asan-ubsan
testPresets.description: Linux. LeakSanitizer rides along with ASan here and nowhere else, which makes this the only place a leak is caught -- and for a decrypted model, a missed free means plaintext left in the heap. Set explicitly rather than left to the runtime default, because it is load-bearing.

testPresets.name: asan-ubsan-macos
testPresets.description: The same build without detect_leaks: LeakSanitizer is not supported on macOS, and asking for it aborts every test at startup with a message about the platform rather than about the test. Leaks are checked on Linux only, by asan-ubsan.
